_provenance.method: Evaluate the seven pure-data card modules in the captured pre-master bundle, in original bundle order. Stock fixture and RNG counters are unchanged.

cards.name: Strike
cards.flavor:
First cut of the hamlets.

Made with whatever edge the hamlet owns. Marl's Hollow sends one climber each winter, chosen at the well, and the chosen spends the last evening at the whetting post learning this and nothing more.

The marked learned a thousand cuts. It did them no good.
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage.

cards.name: Defend
cards.flavor:
First guard of the road.

Two crossed lines upon a cairn stone: hold. Cut by climbers for climbers, before the Burning, when the ring was closed to the unmarked.

The mark does not say what to hold against, nor for how long.
cards.textTemplate: Gain {block} Block.

cards.name: Footwork
cards.flavor:
Steps cut into the road.

Too even to be natural, too worn to be recent. The Forsaken credit them to the climbers before. They run past the farthest point any Forsaken is known to have reached, and some lead onto the viaducts, older than the kingdom.

Climbers before you cut steps. Use them.
cards.textTemplate: Gain {block} Block. Draw {draw} card.

cards.name: Evasive Guard
cards.flavor:
Sidestep of the Pale Marches ice-fishers.

The lakes have not thawed since the Burning. The ice cracks all the year round, and gives only beneath a second pair of feet; the fishers learned to trust the sound.

Widow Arne of Sallow Lake says the sound changed last winter. She fishes no longer.
cards.textTemplate: Gain {block} Block, then roll to evade: on a success, gain Block equal to the dodge.

cards.name: Dodge Roll
cards.flavor:
Tumble of the ship-breakers.

Learned upon hulls that shift with every tide at the Grave of Ships. The hulls were already rotting at anchor when the trade stopped, and on the night of the Burning, every hold went warm at once.

Gull-Bet's gang opened the holds the following spring. She has not said what was inside.
cards.textTemplate: Roll to evade: on a success, gain Block from the dodge. Light: 1 Stamina. Medium: 1 Stamina, 1 Energy. Heavy: 2 Stamina, 1 Energy.

cards.name: Gorefire Slash
cards.flavor:
Art of the sellswords of the Bastion.

The hired blades who held the Fell Courtyard wetted their steel with their own blood before each watch, for the Gorefire takes more readily to a blade already red.

The Wardens called it discipline. The sellswords knew it as a price, paid in advance.
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage. Apply {bleed} Bleed.

cards.name: Crimson Cleave
cards.flavor:
Wide cut of the Fell Courtyard watch.

Taught for a gate choked with bodies. On the night the Bastion burned, the dead came up the Muster Stair in numbers the watch had no word for, and this was the only answer it had.

The gate log names the watch whole at the bell. Its hand changes halfway down the page.
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage to ALL enemies. Apply {bleed} Bleed to ALL.

cards.name: Shield Bash
cards.flavor:
Rim-strike of the Wardens' shield line.

Drilled in the years of the Spring Wars, when envoys of the Northern Holds came to the Bastion gate to haggle the price of a spring. The Wardens struck with the rim, for the face bore the gilded crest.

Twice the Holds were struck. Twice they paid.
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage and {poiseDamage} Poise damage.

cards.name: Quickstep
cards.flavor:
Footwork of the Bastion's hired blades.

After the Burning the weald's spring would not turn, and green came up between the courtyard flags. The sellswords learned short, flat steps upon the moss. The Wardens, who never stood where the footing was worst, did not.

The steps are counted to a dawn peal that brings no dawn.
cards.textTemplate: Gain {block} Block. Draw {draw} card.

cards.name: Guard Counter
cards.flavor:
Riposte of the sworn Wardens.

The enemy commits; the Bastion answers, and its answer is always the greater. So the Wardens taught the drill, and so they told of the Spring Wars, in which they claimed never to have struck first.

The Northern Holds remember it otherwise.
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage. If you have Block: deal {damage.2} instead.

cards.name: Iron Resolve
cards.flavor:
Standing order of the Bastion.

Read at the muster peal: a Warden holds until relieved, and relief comes by the bell. The bell-roll kept the names of all who held.

After the Burning, the roll runs on for many pages, in a hand no scribe knew, bearing names no Warden ever enlisted.
cards.textTemplate: Gain {block} Block. If in Bulwark Stance: gain {block.2} instead.

cards.name: Serrated Blade
cards.flavor:
Saw-backed blade from the forges beneath the Bastion ridge.

Weald smiths filed its teeth for clearing briar, and the Wardens took it up when the Blight came out of the woods. The smiths were never paid for the change of use.

How the briar learned to bleed, the smiths will not speak of.
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage. If the target has Bleed: apply {bleed} more Bleed.

cards.name: Enter: Gorefire
cards.flavor:
The breaking stance, first of the Wardens' two.

The drill is to hold the flame in the blade, not the hand. Sergeants warned that the stance takes the hand if held too long. Sellswords held it longest of all, which the Wardens took for greed.

Hold the flame in the blade; it still takes the hand.
cards.textTemplate: Enter Gorefire Stance. Draw {draw} card.

cards.name: Enter: Bulwark
cards.flavor:
The holding stance, second of the Wardens' two.

Low and square, shield set to the hinge side. The Wardens called the gate a wall a man could carry, and held that no gate kept in this stance had ever fallen.

That teaching was set down before the Burning, and was never amended.
cards.textTemplate: Enter Bulwark Stance.

upgrade.textTemplate: Enter Bulwark Stance. Gain {block} extra Block.

cards.name: Riposte
cards.flavor:
Return off the guard, as the Citadel fencing-masters taught it.

The Court held it too fine for field-born hands. Its manual shows a bout upon the bridges in the first year of the Mark Trade, a Knight against an unnamed Warden, and declares the Knight victorious.

In the illustration, the Knight lies upon his back.
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage. If you have Block: deal {poiseDamage} Poise damage.

cards.name: Rend
cards.flavor:
Tearing cut for the rot of the weald.

Written into the field-book after the Burning, by whoever keeps it now. It bids the reader cut the rot from hound and hamlet folk alike, for the rot came up the river road with the Court's traders.

The ink is fresh. The hand shakes.
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage. Apply {bleed} Bleed. Gorefire: apply {bleed.2} more.

cards.name: Cleaving Blow
cards.flavor:
Heavy sweep of the weald hamlets.

Learned by watching the Wardens from beyond the walls, for no Warden would teach the unmarked. It is swung in the winters when blight-hounds come down out of the lanternwood in packs.

The Wardens called the weald their charge. The hamlets paid for that charge in spring grain.
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage to ALL enemies. Deal {poiseDamage} Poise damage to ALL.

cards.name: Stomp
cards.flavor:
Heel-strike of the Fell Courtyard.

The Wardens named it unworthy and used it all the same, for in the courtyard the fallen seldom stayed down. Sellswords held that the Wardens objected only to being seen at it.

Many an old Bastion helm bears the dent of a heel.
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage and {poiseDamage} Poise damage.

cards.name: Rallying Standard
cards.flavor:
Banner of the Bastion muster.

Raised when the bell rang the line into place. The drill ends thus: raise the standard, sound the bell, log that the line held.

The final muster is logged as held, at dawn. The Bastion has seen no dawn since the Burning.
cards.textTemplate: At the start of your turn, gain 1 Strength and take 1 damage.

upgrade.textTemplate: At the start of your turn, gain 1 Strength.

cards.name: War Surgeon
cards.flavor:
Field practice of the Bastion's surgeon-wardens.

They stitched wounds upon the wall, never below it, for a Warden stitched standing remained a Warden, and one carried to the stool was struck from the roll. The Wardens claimed their surgeons outdid the Chapel's physicians.

The Chapel's own figures burned with the Chapel.
cards.textTemplate: Heal 2 HP for every 4 Bleed on all enemies. Exhaust.

upgrade.textTemplate: Heal 2 HP for every 3 Bleed on all enemies. Exhaust.

cards.name: Hemorrhage
cards.flavor:
Second cut, laid into an open wound.

The Court's surgeons, who studied such matters, recorded that Wardens bled longer than other men beneath the knife, and blamed the thinness of field-born blood. The finding was signed by the surgeons as one body.

No cases were attached to it.
cards.textTemplate: Double the target's Bleed. Exhaust.

upgrade.textTemplate: Double the target's Bleed.

cards.name: Twinblade Flurry
cards.flavor:
Two short blades, worked in turn, as the weald's sellswords used them.

Too poor for a shield and too proud to carry a Warden's, they were hired for the Bastion's narrow gates. It is said part of their wage was paid in marks rather than coin: a right to the city's warmth.

Those who refused the mark are the ones who tell of it.
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage {hits} times.

cards.name: Shieldwall
cards.flavor:
Formation of the Bastion's shield line.

Rim locked to rim across the Fell Courtyard. The Wardens credited it with holding the gate through three hungry winters of the Spring Wars, when Hold petitioners camped below the walls.

The field-book enters the price of spring in the same column as the petitioners turned away.
cards.textTemplate: Gain {block} Block. If in Bulwark Stance: gain 4 Block next turn.

cards.name: Kick Off
cards.flavor:
Boot-strike of the Muster Stair.

Sellswords learned it upon steps steep enough that the fall does the killing. The Wardens forbade it as common, and had adopted it within a season.

What is kicked from the stair now climbs it again.
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage and {poiseDamage} Poise damage. Exhaust.

upgrade.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage and {poiseDamage} Poise damage.

cards.name: Warding Lunge
cards.flavor:
Guarded advance into the breaking stance.

Taught as the moment to cease holding and begin taking ground. The Warden was to know that moment by the bell. When the Bellfoundry bell cracked, a new line was added beneath.

Know it by the smell of the courtyard.
cards.textTemplate: Gain {block} Block. Enter Gorefire Stance.

cards.name: Impale
cards.flavor:
Pinning thrust of the weald hamlets.

Learned in the first winter of the Blight, against what rose from the drowned hamlet and would not stay down. A pinned thing stops, the hamlets say. The Wardens would once have burned such things.

But the fire went into the Wardens that winter.
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage. If the target is Staggered: apply {bleed} Bleed.

cards.name: Warcry
cards.flavor:
The bell-roll, shouted.

A custom of the gates farthest from the Bellfoundry, where the bell could not be heard. The Wardens held that the roll bore power of its own if read in order. Sellswords, who were not on it, shouted it all the same.

It is said the Bell Keeper answers, with a cracked bell.
cards.textTemplate: Gain {strength} Strength. Draw {draw} card. Exhaust.

upgrade.textTemplate: Gain {strength} Strength. Draw {draw} card.

cards.name: Executioner
cards.flavor:
Finishing blow of the Fell Warden.

Taught before his leg went the way of the weald and his blade was ground into a cane. The field-book holds that he never struck a man already kneeling.

The last page in his hand, dated the night of the Burning, is a list of kneeling men.
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage. If the target is Staggered: deal {damage.2} instead.

cards.name: Goreblood
cards.flavor:
The Wardens' name for blood-madness.

The state in which a fighter has spilled enough of their own blood that fear no longer holds. In sworn men the Wardens called it virtue; in sellswords, vice. The two are described in the same words.

Its only instruction: keep standing.
cards.textTemplate: Poise thresholds no longer increase after filling.

cards.name: Unbreakable
cards.flavor:
Order to hold the Fell Courtyard gate.

Dated, signed and never countermanded. The gate log continues past the Burning in a second hand, one entry each night, at the same hour. The gate still stands; the wall on either side does not.

No relief is recorded.
cards.textTemplate: Block no longer expires at the start of your turn. (Block capped at 30.)

upgrade.textTemplate: Block no longer expires at the start of your turn. (Block capped at 40.)

cards.name: Stitched Arms
cards.flavor:
Swordwork of the Court's stitched knights.

After the Court Flame died, the surgeons sewed the knights to their swords, that no oath might be set down. The Citadel's record names it an honour: a knight's word made flesh.

The record was written by the surgeons.
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage to a random enemy, scaling with Energy spent.

upgrade.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage to a random enemy, scaling with Energy spent.

cards.name: Last Stand
cards.flavor:
Final entry of the Fell Courtyard gate log.

One gate, one man, it reads. The man is not named, as though the writer thought none would need it.

The dead are counted twice upon the page, and the counts do not agree.
cards.textTemplate: Ethereal. Gain Block equal to your missing HP (max 20).

upgrade.textTemplate: Ethereal. Gain Block equal to your missing HP (max 30).

cards.name: Warrior's Vow
cards.flavor:
Contract of the sellswords of the Fell Courtyard.

Hold the gate until relieved; pay in advance. The weald's hired blades held a paid contract sacred, having few other sacred things, and the Wardens despised them for it.

The last was signed the week before the Burning. Its date of release is blank.
cards.textTemplate: Innate. Enter Gorefire Stance. Exhaust.

upgrade.textTemplate: Innate. Enter Gorefire Stance. Draw {draw} card. Exhaust.

cards.name: Ruinous Blow
cards.flavor:
Whole-body blow of the Wardens.

Reserved for a gate where all else has failed, and called a Warden's last argument. What becomes of the Warden who makes it, the drill does not say.

The pages that follow are stained through.
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage and {poiseDamage} Poise damage.

cards.name: Bloodhunter's Strike
cards.flavor:
Strike of the Bastion kennels.

Taught by the kennelmaster before the hounds turned. The kennel book names them the finest in the three cities, trained upon the scent of blood alone, and never loosed on the weald's own people.

After the Burning, the hamlets' dogs were found in those same kennels.
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage, plus 1 for each Bleed on the target.

cards.name: Sanguine Pact
cards.flavor:
Soldier's bargain of the Bastion's lesser shrine.

Blood spilled from an enemy is sworn to the one who spilled it. The Wardens thought it a harmless field-born custom, like the harvest tithe. The Chapel called it a mockery of the Writing, and fined the shrine.

The fine was paid. The shrine was in use the night of the Burning.
cards.textTemplate: Whenever Bleed bursts on an enemy, gain 2 Strength.

cards.name: Goreslash
cards.flavor:
Short cut of the Bastion's hired blades.

The sellswords had no patience for the Wardens' long forms. A long cut belongs in songs, they said, and the songs of the Bastion were paid for by the Wardens.

The sellswords kept a verse of their own. Only its tune survives.
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage. Apply {bleed} Bleed.

cards.name: Bracing Stance
cards.flavor:
First stance of the Bastion recruit.

Feet planted, shield braced against the Bastion's own wall, before either true stance was taught. Drillmaster Hask taught it thirty winters.

Her last entry is a roll of recruits, every name struck through but one, and that one scraped away.
cards.textTemplate: Gain {block} Block. If in Bulwark Stance: gain {block.2} more.

cards.name: Flame to Blade
cards.flavor:
Lanternwood oil, set alight upon the edge.

A late practice of the Wardens, adopted when plain steel no longer frightened what came out of the weald. The Chapel frowned upon Wardens bearing fire they had not been given.

Mind the sleeve; the oil takes it before the enemy.
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage. If already in Gorefire Stance: deal {damage.2} more. Enter Gorefire Stance.

cards.name: Iron Vow
cards.flavor:
Oath of the Wardens, sworn with the sword hand upon the gate.

Sworn Wardens bore the flame-mark from birth, and the oath was laid over it as a second promise. Sellswords swore it with no first promise beneath, and so the Wardens held them less bound.

What that meant on the night of the Burning, no oath foretold.
cards.textTemplate: Whenever you lose HP, gain 3 Block.

cards.name: Blood Tithe
cards.flavor:
Harvest tithe of the weald, paid in blood.

Given at the Bastion's field-shrine in years the grain failed. The Wardens called it voluntary, and kept no names, as a courtesy to the givers.

The tithe-roll lengthens with each year of the Mark Trade, and the villages it lists grow fewer.
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage, plus double the Bleed on the target.

cards.name: Poise Breaker
cards.flavor:
Knee-strike of Drillmaster Hask.

Her answer to anything larger than a Warden: a knight and a kennel hound, she wrote, bend at the same place. She drew them both.

Beside them, in later ink, a third figure grown of briar, under a name found nowhere else in the book.
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage and {poiseDamage} Poise damage. If the target is Staggered: deal {poiseDamage.2} more Poise damage.

cards.name: Rondel Parry
cards.flavor:
Parry upon the guard of a rondel dagger.

Favoured by the Bastion's older sellswords, who kept the short blade long after the Wardens ceased to issue it. The rondels came from the Northern Holds as tribute, and were worth more than a season's wage.

They bear a crest no herald of the ring recorded.
cards.textTemplate: Gain {block} Block and deal {poiseDamage} Poise damage.

cards.name: Sunderplate
cards.flavor:
Joint-splitting blow of the Wardens.

Devised in the years of the Mark Trade with the Court's knights in mind, lest the Court forget which flame kept it fed. No occasion of its use is recorded.

Beside the drill, a knight's gorget, its crest scratched out.
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage and {poiseDamage} Poise damage. If the target is Staggered: apply {bleed} Bleed.

cards.name: Brace
cards.flavor:
The crouch before either stance.

Knees bent, weight low, the body made ready to be struck. The field-book gives it the first page, and calls it the one lesson all Wardens learned alike, sworn or hired, marked or not.

A later hand has corrected it.
cards.textTemplate: Enter Brace Stance.

upgrade.textTemplate: Enter Brace Stance. Gain {block} Block.

cards.name: Hewing Arc
cards.flavor:
A wide cut that opens old wounds.

Taught in the Vanguard's yard to recruits who had never held a blade. The sergeants said the arc forgives a poor grip, and the Gorefire does the rest.

The yard is ash now. The recruits still swing it wide, as they were shown.
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage. If in Gorefire Stance: apply {bleed} Bleed.

cards.name: Sundering Chop
cards.flavor:
Downward blow meant to split a shield.

The Vanguard's smiths measured their work by it. A shield that survived three chops was sent to the wall; one that did not was sent back to the forge with the smith's name chalked upon it.

Few names were chalked twice.
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage and {poiseDamage} Poise damage. Draw {draw} card.

cards.name: Set the Shield
cards.flavor:
The rim planted, the shoulder behind it.

Old Vanguard drill: the shield is set before the enemy is seen, and the man behind it waits. The drill was called cowardice by the Court's duellists, until the night the Court's gate fell.

The duellists did not drill again.
cards.textTemplate: Gain {block} Block. Enter Bulwark Stance.

cards.name: Aegis of Embers
cards.flavor:
A shield held into the fire until it glows.

The last captain of the Vanguard held the causeway so through the whole of the Burning. His shield was found welded to the stones, and his arm was not found at all.

The stones there are warm still, and soldiers kneel on them.
cards.textTemplate: Gain {block} Block. If in Bulwark Stance: gain {strength} Strength.

cards.name: Shield Crash
cards.flavor:
The whole weight of the wall, thrown forward.

A Vanguard shieldman who has held long enough may drive his shield into the line before him. The chronicles of the siege praise it; the surgeons who reset the shieldmen's shoulders afterward do not.

Both kept their records honestly.
cards.textTemplate: Gain {block} Block. Deal damage equal to your Block.

cards.name: Starstone Pebble
cards.flavor:
Chip of catalogued starstone.

Such stones were weighed and numbered by the Observatory's apprentices in their first winter. The Astronomer held them inert once cooled, and wrote as much throughout his catalogue.

Yet frost formed upon their labels by night. Never upon the stones.
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage. Starstone: deal {damage.2} more.

cards.name: Comet Fragment
cards.flavor:
Sorcery of the Starwatch, the first permitted beyond the lens gallery.

Fragments came up the Basalt Stair in miners' sacks, sold by weight, and the Astronomer catalogued every one. Chart 41 records a fall. Chart 42 records a hearth.

Of what lay between, the catalogue is silent.
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage.

cards.name: Starblade Phalanx
cards.flavor:
Blades ground from a single stone.

The apprentices found that blades from one stone answered one another in sequence, the second truer than the first. The Chapel's censor struck "answered" from the record and wrote "rang".

The apprentices kept the first word.
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage. Starstone: deal {damage.2} again.

cards.name: Crystal Barrier
cards.flavor:
Pane of starstone, cut as the great lens was cut.

The great lens cracked in the frost of the eclipse, yet held the light. The Astronomer credited his grinding.

Maud Vell, who ground it, said the crack had closed a little by morning. She would not grind another.
cards.textTemplate: Gain {block} Block. Starstone: {block.2} more.

cards.name: Star Shower
cards.flavor:
Sorcery of the Starwatch, called in sequence.

The log of one autumn vigil counts forty small falls in a single night, none of which reached the ground warm. An apprentice asked in the margin whence forty falls could come.

The answer, in the Astronomer's hand, was cut from the page.
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage {hits} times. Starstone: one more hit of {damage.2}.

cards.name: Scholar's Insight
cards.flavor:
Discipline of the double copy.

Apprentices copied each chart twice, for the second copy is the true one. The two copies of chart 9 differ in a single figure: the distance from the three hearths to a point upon the coast.

Both copies left the Observatory with the apprentice who took the charts.
cards.textTemplate: Draw {draw} cards.

cards.name: Frost Veil
cards.flavor:
Rime drawn over the body.

First seen upon the Observatory's upper terrace on the night of the eclipse, when the terrace froze in the space of a breath and every instrument stopped. The apprentice Hollis logged the hour, and wrote that he did not trust it.

The hour has since been corrected, in an unknown hand.
cards.textTemplate: Gain {block} Block. Apply {frost} Frost.

cards.name: Star Slicer
cards.flavor:
Starstone, split along its grain.

The stone parts cleanly along lines the lens-grinders could see and the miners could not. The grinders held that it had been worked before it fell. The Astronomer called this sentimental.

He kept a split fragment upon his desk, its grain turned to the window.
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage {hits} times. Starstone: one more hit of {damage.2}.

cards.name: Starstone Ward
cards.flavor:
Slab of starstone, raised as a shield.

After the fashion of the Observatory's doors, cut by builders whose name the Chapel did not keep. Starstone stays cold where all else warms.

The apprentices believed those doors were not made to open from within.
cards.textTemplate: Gain {block} Block. Starstone: apply {weak} Weak.

cards.name: Starlance
cards.flavor:
Light forced through a starstone lens.

Discovered when the great lens scorched a line across the chart-room table. The Astronomer had the table kept as it was, and recorded that the line ran true to the south-west.

The line has lengthened since.
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage. Starstone: {damage.2} instead.

cards.name: Twinkling
cards.flavor:
Light drawn from a varying star.

The Astronomer recorded its variation nightly for many years, and drew no conclusion, as was his rule. In the last spring before the Burning, he spent three nights upon it alone.

The charts of those nights are not in the series.
cards.textTemplate: Draw {draw} card. Starstone: gain {gainEnergy} Energy.

cards.name: Frost Nova
cards.flavor:
Ring of cold, after the frozen ash of the caldera.

Miners found such rings about fresh falls upon the caldera floor. Coll, a foreman, told the apprentices the ash froze before the stone landed. The Astronomer named miners unreliable witnesses.

He bought Coll's next fragment at double the price.
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage. Apply {frost} Frost. Starstone: apply {frost.2} more.

cards.name: Starstone Arc
cards.flavor:
Arc of force, used to measure the stone's reach.

Measured three times, the stone was found to have moved between readings. The Starwatch recorded an error of the apparatus, and replaced it.

The same error is recorded each month, until the eclipse.
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage. Starstone: apply {vulnerable} Vulnerable.

cards.name: Lucidity
cards.flavor:
Clarity for the work.

Practised on the one clear night in forty the reach allowed. The Astronomer worked such nights without sleep, and bade his apprentices do the same.

They believed he saw more than the charts show, and wrote it elsewhere.
cards.textTemplate: Gain {gainEnergy} Energy. Draw {draw} card.

cards.name: Stargazer
cards.flavor:
The long watch at the eyepiece.

The Astronomer kept it a hundred years by his own count, recording the coal's dimming and never its meaning. The Chapel admired his restraint.

His apprentices believed he watched something he had already resolved not to describe.
cards.textTemplate: At the start of your turn, gain Starstone Charge.

cards.name: Astral Armor
cards.flavor:
Mantle of cold light, after Starwatch Terrace.

The terrace upon the Drowned Coast was paved in starstone, that the apprentices might measure the new tower's draw. The paving never warmed, and the salt spray never dried upon it.

A Saint was sent to bless the stones. She asked to be posted elsewhere.
cards.textTemplate: At the end of your turn, gain 4 Block.

upgrade.textTemplate: At the end of your turn, gain 8 Block.

cards.name: Moonrend Cut
cards.flavor:
Crescent stroke of the Observatory's night-porters.

The porters walked the Basalt Stair with lanterns and curved blades, and claimed the moon's passage over the caldera showed them where to cut. The Starwatch called it folklore, and employed them regardless.

Their blades are found in the lower galleries, in hands no longer quite their own.
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage and {poiseDamage} Poise damage.

cards.name: Meteorite
cards.flavor:
Heavy fall, called upon one enemy.

The largest fragment the Starwatch recovered weighed more than its size allowed. The miners who carried it said it weighed more atop the stair than at its foot.

The Astronomer had it weighed at both ends, and recorded the results in cipher.
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage. Starstone: {damage.2} instead.

cards.name: Meteor Swarm
cards.flavor:
Many falls, called as one.

Chart 43 records two falls in a single night. Miners were sent to both sites and found no crater at either. The Astronomer entered both regardless, for his lens could not err.

A third mark on chart 43, in another ink, is nowhere explained.
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage to ALL enemies. Starstone: {damage.2} again.

cards.name: Gravity Well
cards.flavor:
Pull of the Observatory's great pendulum.

The pendulum swung true for most of the Starwatch's history. In the years the Spire was built, it leaned toward the coast, and did not recover.

The Astronomer ordered the foundations inspected. The report is blank.
cards.textTemplate: Apply {vulnerable} Vulnerable to ALL enemies. Starstone: apply {weak} Weak to ALL.

cards.name: Azure Coil
cards.flavor:
Blue light that gathers about the working.

First seen around apprentices reciting the star tables aloud in rhythm. The Chapel's censor ruled the tables were written in an old script, and forbade their recitation.

The coil returned the following night.
cards.textTemplate: Whenever you play a Skill, gain 2 Block.

cards.name: Astral Cleave
cards.flavor:
Cut of cold force.

First seen when a falling fragment passed through the lens gallery and sheared the telescope in two before cooling upon the floor. The Astronomer recorded a fall. Maud Vell, at the eyepiece, called it a throw.

She was dismissed at the season's end.
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage and {poiseDamage} Poise damage. Starstone: deal {damage.2} more.

cards.name: Radiant Spray
cards.flavor:
Flare cast wide.

In the years the Spire was built, a flare lit every terrace of the Observatory at once, and the apprentices on watch lost their sight for days. The log gives no source.

When their sight returned, they were asked not to speak of it.
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} to ALL enemies. Apply {vulnerable} Vulnerable to ALL. Starstone: deal {damage.2} to ALL again.

cards.name: Supernova
cards.flavor:
Brightest working in the charts.

The final predictive chart forecasts a light great enough to burn the paper it is drawn upon. The Starwatch took it for the fate of a star.

The chart is unsigned and undated. The apprentices swore it was not among the sheets they left upon his desk.
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage to ALL enemies, scaling with Energy spent.

upgrade.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage to ALL enemies, scaling with Energy spent.

cards.name: Time Dilation
cards.flavor:
Slowing of the moment, after the eclipse.

By the Starwatch's reckoning the eclipse lasted a single night. By the Observatory clock, it has not ended. Anselm, keeper of the clock, refused to reset it.

He was found beside it, standing as he stood when the light went.
cards.textTemplate: Gain {gainEnergy} Energy. Draw {draw} cards. Exhaust.

upgrade.textTemplate: Gain {gainEnergy} Energy. Draw {draw} cards.

cards.name: Starstone Kris
cards.flavor:
Wavy dagger of starstone.

Carried by apprentices for rough work in the lower galleries. Its first owner wrapped it in cloth and found the cloth frosted by morning. The kris keeps its cold whether carried or not.

It was coldest, the apprentice noted, in the Astronomer's presence.
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage. Starstone: draw {draw} card and deal {damage.2} again.

cards.name: Constellation
cards.flavor:
Sorcery of three stars, after the Goldbough crest.

Three flames upon three twigs. The Chapel taught that the crest came first, and the stars were named for it.

The Starwatch's oldest plate, cut before the kingdom, shows the same three stars, and a faint fourth. The Chapel's copy omits it.
cards.textTemplate: Whenever you gain Starstone Charge, deal 4 damage to a random enemy.

cards.name: Starfall Beam
cards.flavor:
Column of falling light.

Modelled upon a fall the Astronomer charted in advance. He foresaw where it would strike upon the caldera rim, and sent no warning to the mine camps there, for they were unmarked, and absent from the Court's maps.

His margin gives the fall's weight to the grain. Of the camps, nothing.
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage to ALL enemies. Starstone: {damage.2} instead.

cards.name: Starcaller
cards.flavor:
Many falls, called in rhythm.

The apprentices chanted the star tables while practising it in the lens gallery, and on the night it was first attempted, eleven falls were recorded. The Astronomer entered chant and falls upon the same line.

He drew no connection between them. He drew none between anything.
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage, scaling with Energy spent. Starstone: deal {damage.2} more.

upgrade.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage, scaling with Energy spent. Starstone: deal {damage.2} more.

cards.name: Umbral Ward
cards.flavor:
Ward of shadow, after the eclipse.

During the eclipse the Observatory cast no shadow, which the Starwatch recorded as a curiosity of the light. The apprentices upon the terrace cast shadows as ever.

Theirs fell toward the Observatory, not away.
cards.textTemplate: Gain {block} Block. Starstone: {block.2} instead.

cards.name: Waxing Moon
cards.flavor:
Sorcery of the Starwatch, drawn from the moon-table.

In the last years before the Burning, the Astronomer observed that as the moon waxed, the coal in the Crown dimmed in equal measure. He named it coincidence, and kept the moon-table no longer.

What he would not record, his apprentices remembered.
cards.textTemplate: At the start of your turn, apply 2 Vulnerable to ALL enemies.

cards.name: Shooting Shard
cards.flavor:
Small fall, too faint for the charts.

The Starwatch left such falls unrecorded, a star too faint to mark the lens being unworthy of ink. The reach miners kept their own tally, scratched upon the walls of the lower galleries.

Their count runs far higher.
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage. Starstone: deal {damage.2} more.

cards.name: Warding Star
cards.flavor:
Guarding light, after the Fixed Lamp.

A star above the coast that did not move with the others. The Starwatch took it for a flaw of the lens and reground the lens twice. The star remained.

After the Spire was finished, the log names it only "the error".
cards.textTemplate: Gain {block} Block. Starstone: draw {draw} card.

cards.name: Star Path
cards.flavor:
Step along a line of light.

The fourth viaduct spur appears upon the Starwatch's charts years before the Court commissioned it, drawn in the Astronomer's hand from the ring to the coast. The Court later claimed the Spire as its own design.

Who showed the Astronomer where to draw, the charts do not tell.
cards.textTemplate: Draw {draw} card. Starstone: draw {draw.2} more.

cards.name: Moonlit Shield
cards.flavor:
Frost raised by moonlight upon starstone.

It rises along the rails of Starwatch Terrace on clear nights, where the apprentices once judged the cold by it. From the Tidebound Chapel across the water, the salt-priests have watched it form the shape of a word.

They have not written it down.
cards.textTemplate: Whenever you gain Starstone Charge, gain 3 Block.

cards.name: Celestial Lance
cards.flavor:
Spear of light, horizon to zenith.

Chart 58 records such a line, lasting a single breath, sourced to a star upon no other chart. The Astronomer entered it as a fault of optics, then spent a week grinding a new lens he was never seen to use.

Chart 58 is the last he signed.
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage. Starstone: {damage.2} instead.

cards.name: Astromancer
cards.flavor:
The Starwatch's discipline, carried away.

An apprentice took the charts and left the Observatory before the eclipse. The Starwatch recorded it as theft. The apprentice's line in the roll has been scraped away.

Not so thoroughly that the name cannot be guessed.
cards.textTemplate: At the start of your turn, gain Starstone Charge and draw a card.

cards.name: Star Spark
cards.flavor:
Spark struck from a starstone flint.

The chart room kept such a flint for its lamps, for the Astronomer would not suffer the Chapel's flame in that room. Its sparks died before they landed.

Maud Vell said the stone was being careful.
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage. Starstone: apply {weak} Weak.

cards.name: Astral Insight
cards.flavor:
Clear sight into the charts.

The apprentices believed the Starwatch's ledgers were meant to end where the charts of the fourth hearth began. There the Astronomer once underlined a line, and later struck through his own mark.

The charts of the fourth hearth were not among those carried away.
cards.textTemplate: Gain {block} Block. Draw {draw} card. Starstone: draw {draw.2} more.

cards.name: Attune
cards.flavor:
First exercise of the apprentice.

Hold the stone until pulse and rhythm match. The Starwatch taught that starstone answers rhythm, not force, and credited the principle to the Astronomer.

The standing stones upon the marches road hum in the same rhythm. They are older than he.
cards.textTemplate: Restore {restoreMana} Mana. Exhaust.

upgrade.textTemplate: Restore {restoreMana} Mana.

cards.name: Cinder Sigil
cards.flavor:
A star traced in hot ash.

The Observatory's apprentices drew them on the terrace to fix a sighting, and swept them away at dawn. After the eclipse the sigils would not sweep; they had burned into the stone.

The terrace is covered in them now, none drawn by hand.
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage. Starstone: apply {burn} Burn.

cards.name: Ashen Mote
cards.flavor:
A fleck of burnt chart, flung like a star.

When the Observatory's archive burned, the apprentice Hollis gathered its ash in jars, believing the charts might be read again. Some of it could be.

It reads the same sky, though not the one above the Observatory.
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage. Starstone: deal {damage.2} more.

cards.name: Ember Vigil
cards.flavor:
A coal kept through the cloudy night.

On nights the reach would not clear, the Astronomer bade one apprentice keep an ember lit beneath the great lens, lest the lens forget warmth. None knew what he meant.

The lens was cold the morning after the eclipse. The apprentice was gone.
cards.textTemplate: Gain {block} Block. Starstone: draw {draw} card.

cards.name: Read the Ash
cards.flavor:
Divination by what the fire left behind.

A practice the Astronomer forbade as superstition, and the apprentices kept in secret beneath the terrace stair. They burned a copy of each night's chart and read the ash against it.

The two agreed more often than the Astronomer would have liked.
cards.textTemplate: Draw {draw} cards.

cards.name: Pyre of Charts
cards.flavor:
The catalogue given to the flame at once.

When the Starwatch came for the Observatory's records, the apprentices burned them in the courtyard rather than surrender them. The fire rose higher than the tower.

The Starwatch recorded the fire as a new star, and catalogued it.
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage to ALL enemies. Starstone: apply {burn} Burn to ALL.

cards.name: Ash Circle
cards.flavor:
A ring of ash poured round the feet.

The apprentices drew one about the great lens each eclipse, to keep the dark from settling on the glass. On the last eclipse the ring was drawn, and the dark settled elsewhere.

Nobody inside the ring was harmed. Nobody outside it was found.
cards.textTemplate: Gain {block} Block. Starstone: apply {weak} Weak to ALL enemies.

cards.name: Kindled Omen
cards.flavor:
A sign read in sparks, then set upon a foe.

The apprentices threw pinches of ash into the brazier and named the shapes the sparks made. Most were nothing. A few were names of the living.

Those whose names were read seldom lived the year, and the practice was stopped.
cards.textTemplate: Apply {vulnerable} Vulnerable and {burn} Burn. Starstone: draw {draw} card.

cards.name: Cinder Lance
cards.flavor:
A shaft of burning ash, cold at its point.

The Astronomer's first experiment with the ash of starstone, logged as a failure: the ash burned without heat. His apprentices kept the log.

Where the lance struck the Observatory's wall, frost still forms each night.
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage. Starstone: apply {frost} Frost.

cards.name: Ashfall Rite
cards.flavor:
The sky asked to rain ash, and answering.

The rite is recorded once, in Hollis's hand, on the night after the eclipse. It names no author. It names the Observatory as the altar, and the reach as the congregation.

The reach has been grey since, and is said to be listening.
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage to ALL enemies {hits} times. Starstone: apply {burn} Burn to ALL.

cards.name: Phoenix Chart
cards.flavor:
A chart that redraws itself from its ash.

One page of the burned catalogue did not stay burned. Each dawn it lay whole in the courtyard, its stars a little moved. The apprentices burned it thrice more.

It returned each time, and each time a little warmer to the touch.
cards.textTemplate: Heal {heal} HP. Gain {block} Block. Exhaust.

cards.name: Pyre Light
cards.flavor:
The last light of a burning star.

The Astronomer claimed a star gives its brightest light as it dies, and that the light can be caught if one is quick. His apprentices thought it a figure of speech.

He was holding a lens when the tower burned. The lens was found.
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage. Starstone: deal {damage.2} more. Exhaust.

cards.name: Rite of Cinders
cards.flavor:
The embers stirred, and the mind with them.

The apprentices performed it before long watches, breathing the smoke of burned charts until the stars came clearer. The Astronomer called it poisoning. He also asked what they saw.

They saw a great deal. Little of it was in the sky.
cards.textTemplate: Gain {gainEnergy} Energy. Draw {draw} cards. Starstone: gain {gainEnergy.2} more Energy. Exhaust.

cards.name: Urgent Heal
cards.flavor:
Rite of the Furnace Chapel, for wounds taken in its service.

Performed swiftly, its prayer cut to the first line. The rubric bids the wound be bound beneath the brand, never over it, that the mark be left clear.

We bind the wound beneath the unspent brand.
cards.textTemplate: Heal {heal} HP.

cards.name: Blood Pact
cards.flavor:
Second office of the birth-rite.

The flame-mark was pressed into the newborn's wrist, and the parents answered in the child's stead. The Chapel called it a promise and a privilege.

In the birth-roll of the crown-born wards, beside the Herald's name, one word is struck through.
cards.textTemplate: Lose {loseHp} HP. Gain {gainEnergy} Energy. Draw {draw} card.

cards.name: Blight Touch
cards.flavor:
Blessing of the Feral Ember.

Taken from the Chapel's blessing of the sick and turned to what the Feral Ember holds its truer purpose: to give warmth and keep no account. The Saints name it heresy.

The converts say the touch is warm. None have said otherwise.
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage. Apply {crimsonBlight} Crimson Blight.

cards.name: Flagellation
cards.flavor:
Penance of the Chapel's novices.

Performed with a knotted cord upon the bare back. The Saints taught that pain offered freely spares the fire the trouble of taking it. Novice Wen kept the penance daily for three years.

She wrote that she could not say whom it had spared.
cards.textTemplate: Lose {loseHp} HP. Deal {damage} damage.

cards.name: Penance
cards.flavor:
Kneeling upon the cold stone of the nave.

Prescribed for small failings of devotion, until the knees bled. The nave was repaved twice in the years of the Mark Trade, with stone from the caldera, and no reason given.

We kneel on the cold stone and are forgiven.
cards.textTemplate: Gain {block} Block. Heal {heal} HP.

cards.name: Litany
cards.flavor:
Closing prayer of the funeral rite.

Spoken over the ledger once a name was entered, and said to return a share of warmth to the mourners. Novices learned it before they could read. The last novice says it each night.

The ledger was lost in the Burning. There is no name to close.
cards.textTemplate: Apply {weak} Weak and {insanity} Insanity.

cards.name: Grave Offering
cards.flavor:
Offering at the graves of the crown-born.

Upon the anniversary of their writing, mourners opened the grave and set a coal beside what remained. The Chapel ended the rite in the years of the Marking, saying the dead no longer needed company.

By then, the mourners had found the graves colder than they ought to be.
cards.textTemplate: Lose {loseHp} HP. Deal {damage} damage to ALL enemies.

cards.name: Bloodletting
cards.flavor:
Bleeding before the blessing of bread.

The Saints bled into the bowl first, that nothing be taken from the congregation the Saint had not first given. The Chapel taught it as humility.

On the days of the rite, the bread ran short, and the Saints ate first.
cards.textTemplate: Lose {loseHp} HP. Gain {block} Block.

cards.name: Contagion
cards.flavor:
Communion of the Feral Ember.

The Chapel passed one cup along the pews, that the congregation be one body before the fire. The Feral Ember revived the rite with another cup.

We pass one cup along the pews, and every mouth is red.
cards.textTemplate: Apply {crimsonBlight} Crimson Blight to ALL enemies.

cards.name: Cull the Weak
cards.flavor:
Rite of gathering the failing.

Performed in the sick-wards of the crown-born, that the dying need not linger. The Wandering Physician, who served in those wards, kept his own list of those gathered. The ward rolls name none of them.

Many he had expected to recover.
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage. If the target has Crimson Blight: deal {damage.2} more.

cards.name: Transfusion
cards.flavor:
Communion of blood, between Saint and dying.

Blood poured from cup to cup, for the dying of good family. The rubric speaks of the Saint giving, never receiving. Novice Wen wrote that the flow ran both ways.

The Saints rose from the rite looking younger.
cards.textTemplate: Heal {heal} HP.

cards.name: Blightward
cards.flavor:
Cloth laid over an unfinished brand.

Begun for the Herald, whose mark began to burn on the night of the Burning and stopped partway. The Chapel remnant now lays such cloths over the brands of its dead, and teaches that the fire will return to finish its work.

The fire started on me and stopped. I do not know why.
cards.textTemplate: Gain {block} Block. If below half HP: gain {block.2} more.

cards.name: Martyr's Blood
cards.flavor:
Offering of the Saint's own blood.

Made at the altar when the censer ran low, for a Saint's blood was held to burn hotter than any incense. When the censers were cleaned in the years of the Spire, dried blood lay layered beneath the ash.

We spend ourselves at the altar, and the censer swings faster.
cards.textTemplate: Lose {loseHp} HP. Gain {gainEnergy} Energy. Draw {draw} cards. Exhaust.

cards.name: Blight Bloom
cards.flavor:
Red flowers upon the graves of the crown-born.

They first appeared in the Furnace Chapel's garden in the Long Winter. The remnant tends them as a sign that the dead are giving yet.

They spread fastest where the earth is freshly turned. The remnant has begun turning more.
cards.textTemplate: Double the target's Crimson Blight. Exhaust.

upgrade.textTemplate: Double the target's Crimson Blight.

cards.name: Sacred Harvest
cards.flavor:
Harvest rite of the Chapel.

A gilded sickle, blessed and carried through the fields of the crown-born. The Chapel found the harvest beautiful, and built a chapel to it. The rubric lists what the sickle is to cut, in the fields and after.

The second half of the list is written in the old script.
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage. Heal {heal} HP.

cards.name: Thorn Halo
cards.flavor:
Crown of briar, worn at the feast of the Founding.

In memory of the first Saint, who by Chapel tradition wore thorns in the caldera; each thorn stood for a name carried. In the Long Winter, the Thorn Matriarch grew a crown of her own.

The remnant counts her a Saint. She was a Warden, and never swore to them.
cards.textTemplate: At the start of your turn, apply 1 Crimson Blight to ALL enemies.

cards.name: Communion
cards.flavor:
Sharing of warmth, as kept at the Tidebound Chapel.

The Saints raised that chapel upon the Drowned Coast to keep watch upon the Spire, which they called heresy. Its congregation shrank with each winter after the Spire was finished.

We watched from Tidebound Chapel and never saw the heresy lit.
cards.textTemplate: At the start of your turn, heal 3 HP.

cards.name: Gilded Oath
cards.flavor:
Oath of the Goldbough crest.

A gilded branch, three flames upon three twigs: the kingdom and its hearths. Novices swore it at their first vigil, before they were told what the hearths were fed.

The crest above the Furnace Chapel's nave bears a fourth twig, bare, blamed upon a careless gilder.
cards.textTemplate: Gain {strength} Strength and {dexterity} Dexterity.

cards.name: Plague Bearer
cards.flavor:
Office of the censer-bearer.

The Saints taught that the censer's smoke opened doors to the fire's blessing. When the Chapel set the office down, the Feral Ember took it up, and bears the censers lit through the weald.

The doors open for them more readily than ever they did for the Saints.
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage. Apply {crimsonBlight} Crimson Blight. Draw {draw} card.

cards.name: Exsanguinate
cards.flavor:
Giving of blood, until the giver is light enough to rise.

Performed by the Saints in the last extremity, when a hearth faltered and no other offering remained. The Chapel's record names those who performed it and rose.

The graves assigned to them were found empty.
cards.textTemplate: Lose {loseHp} HP. Deal {damage} damage.

cards.name: Stigmata
cards.flavor:
Marks of the Saints.

Worn openly upon hands and brow, and held by the Chapel to be a favour of the fire. Novices learned they appeared more reliably upon Saints with a knife at hand.

Novice Wen wrote so plainly, then begged forgiveness for it, twice.
cards.textTemplate: Whenever you lose HP, heal 2 HP.

cards.name: Scourge
cards.flavor:
Penitent's walk down the nave.

Scourge in hand, while the congregation answered each blow. The number of blows was set by the number of names written that season. In the last seasons before the Burning, the rite lasted the night.

We walk the nave with the scourge, and the pews answer.
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage to ALL enemies. Apply {crimsonBlight} Crimson Blight to ALL.

cards.name: Reclamation
cards.flavor:
Return of warmth lent to the dying.

Performed at the deathbed once the name was read, and called a courtesy returned. After the rite the dying were colder, and the Saint warmer.

The rubric closes: do not explain this to the family.
cards.textTemplate: Heal 1 HP for every 2 Crimson Blight on all enemies. Exhaust.

upgrade.textTemplate: Heal 1 HP for every Crimson Blight on all enemies. Exhaust.

cards.name: Second Bloom
cards.flavor:
Rite of recovery, named for the weald's second flowering.

The orchards bloomed a second time in years when the Field Flame burned strong, and the Chapel claimed both the blossom and the healing as its work. Neither has come since the Burning.

The last novice performs the rite regardless, and says it works.
cards.textTemplate: Heal half of your missing HP. Exhaust.

cards.name: Plague of Butterflies
cards.flavor:
Red moths of the Furnace Chapel's ossuary.

They dwelt among the bones for as long as the Chapel kept records, and were called the ossuary's keepers. After the Burning, they left the ossuary for the reach.

We loose the red moths from the ossuary; they know the way.
cards.textTemplate: Lose {loseHp} HP. Apply {crimsonBlight} Crimson Blight to ALL enemies.

cards.name: Life Tithe
cards.flavor:
Tithe of life, owed by each crown-born family.

One day in seven, given to the Chapel's work, as the dead had given all their days. In the years of the Marking, the tithe was extended to newborns, who could not work.

We bring the cradle where the bier once stood.
cards.textTemplate: Whenever an enemy dies, heal 8 HP.

cards.name: Crimson Rite
cards.flavor:
Chalice of the high altar.

Reserved to the Saints. It draws from the Saint as the Saint draws from it. The Furnace Saint performs the rite alone now, and keeps the chalice full.

We drink from the chalice, and it drinks from us.
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage, scaling with Energy spent, then heal 2 per Energy.

upgrade.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage, scaling with Energy spent, then heal 3 per Energy.

cards.name: Blight Nova
cards.flavor:
Reading of every name, aloud and at once.

Composed by the Furnace Saint after the Burning. The novices say it is what the fire did that night, and that the rite exists so it will be remembered. The remnant holds it holiest of the liturgies.

It has never been performed to its end.
cards.textTemplate: Deal damage equal to twice the target's Crimson Blight.

upgrade.textTemplate: Deal damage equal to three times the target's Crimson Blight.

cards.name: Last Rites
cards.flavor:
Rite for those not to be written.

Foreigners, criminals, and in the last years, the bought-marked of whom the Chapel had not been told. The rubric forbids a name upon the headstone, and calls this discretion.

The lower cemetery stands blank by the thousand.
cards.textTemplate: Heal 20% of your max HP. Draw {draw} cards. Exhaust.

upgrade.textTemplate: Heal 20% of your max HP. Draw {draw} cards.

cards.name: Zealotry
cards.flavor:
Creed of the Feral Ember.

Each wound is a door the fire walks through. Its priests bless wounds rather than bind them, and hold that the Chapel knew as much, and hid it behind a ledger.

Its converts do not live long. More come each week.
cards.textTemplate: Whenever you lose HP, deal 3 damage to a random enemy.

cards.name: Blood Harvest
cards.flavor:
Reaping of the field of the marked.

So the liturgy names the gathering of names at the close of a plague year. The Saints went out with sickles and ledgers, and the rite is spoken throughout as thanksgiving.

We reap the field of the marked, and give thanks.
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage to ALL enemies, scaling with Energy spent. Then heal 3 per Energy.

upgrade.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage to ALL enemies, scaling with Energy spent. Then heal 3 per Energy.

cards.name: Pain Offering
cards.flavor:
Small pain, offered in advance.

Taught to crown-born children as good citizenship; the children called it paying early. The habit outlived the Chapel among the Forsaken hamlets, learned from refugees after the Burning.

They keep it without knowing whom they pay.
cards.textTemplate: Lose {loseHp} HP. Deal {damage} damage.

cards.name: Withering Touch
cards.flavor:
Touch that withers growth.

Permitted by the rubric upon the weeds of the weald's field-shrines, and nothing else. In the years the Field Flame dimmed, a clause was added forbidding its use upon crops.

The clause is dated after three harvests had failed, and signed by a Saint absent from the roll of Saints.
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage. Apply {crimsonBlight} Crimson Blight.

cards.name: Desperate Rite
cards.flavor:
Rite for when the bier is already made.

The rubric bids the officiant pray louder, and nothing more. The Saints held that the fire heeds the strength of a voice; the novices, that the rubric was written for the family.

The Herald has performed it upon themselves.
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage. If below half HP: deal {damage.2} instead.

cards.name: Ember Tide
cards.flavor:
The Chapel's name for the night of the Burning.

The night the fire read the names of the crown-born all at once. The novices say the censers swung untouched through it, as the congregation burned around them. The censers of the Furnace Chapel have not stopped since.

We kept the censer swinging when the hearth went dark.
cards.textTemplate: Whenever you heal, gain 1 Strength.

cards.name: Blood Offering
cards.flavor:
Bowl filled with the officiant's own blood.

From the Chapel's first years, when the Saints were few; revived by the Furnace Saint after the Burning, when they were fewer. He performs it daily, and grows thin.

The bowl is always full.
cards.textTemplate: Lose {loseHp} HP. Deal {damage} damage.

cards.name: Harbinger of Blight
cards.flavor:
Title of the Feral Ember's preachers.

The Chapel gave the same name to the novice who walked before a bier with a bell. The Feral Ember holds that the word was never the Chapel's to give, but the fire's.

We go before the fire, and it follows us gladly.
cards.textTemplate: Whenever Crimson Blight is applied to an enemy, heal 1 HP.

cards.name: Blightward Lash
cards.flavor:
Scourge turned upon one's own rot.

A discipline the Herald took up after the Burning: to cut the Blight from their own flesh and turn it outward. The Chapel remnant condemns it as heresy against the fire's gift.

Twice the remnant has sent a novice to ask how it is done.
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage. Apply {crimsonBlight} Crimson Blight. Lose {loseHp} HP.

cards.name: Last Mercy
cards.flavor:
Warming of a dying hand.

The Chapel's nursing sisters did it with a coal wrapped in cloth, that the fire might find the hand gentle. The Wandering Physician learned it from them, and does it without the coal.

It seems to work as well. He cannot say what working means.
cards.textTemplate: Heal {heal} HP. Gain {block} Block.

cards.name: Warm Litany
cards.flavor:
First prayer of the Furnace Chapel's novices.

Said over a small hurt, to keep it warm. The novices were taught its words were older than the Chapel, found by the first Saint cut into the caldera wall.

We give the name. We keep the warmth.
cards.textTemplate: Heal {heal}. Gain {block} Block.

cards.name: Ambush
cards.flavor:
Opening of the frozen docks.

Strike from beneath a bridge, from behind, before the other has decided there is a fight at all. The docks learned it from the Court's surgeons, who walked the bridges by night with their bags, and always arrived first.

Their day-books record house calls, but no houses.
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage. Prepared: deal {damage.2} more. Apply {vulnerable} Vulnerable. Consume Prepared.

cards.name: Shiv
cards.flavor:
Sliver of iron from the rail of the Fourth Bridge.

The ironwork froze brittle the night the Court Flame died. Dock children say the railings were cast from the Court's melted oath-tokens, and so are worth more than any blade in the right hands.

Whose hands are right, the children will not tell.
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage. Exhaust.

cards.name: Smoke Pellet
cards.flavor:
Tallow and ash, rolled in a back room on the Chandlers' Stair.

Sold as lamp-starters. The chandler says the recipe was his grandmother's, taken from a Court surgeon, though in his telling the surgeon is sometimes a knight.

The docks buy more of them each winter.
cards.textTemplate: Gain {block} Block. Become Prepared. Exhaust.

cards.name: Quick Cut
cards.flavor:
Knife-work of the Tollmouth fence.

He pays only for quick cuts, holding that a slow cut is a confession and a quick one an accident. Before the Decree, a dock child caught with a knife was hanged, not branded.

The fence considers that the better age.
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage. Prepared: deal {damage.2} more. Consume Prepared.

cards.name: Feint
cards.flavor:
Oldest trick of the frozen docks.

Eyes on the purse, hand on the knife. The docks say the Court's knights were easily taken, for they had sworn to look wherever a threat was declared.

No such clause appears in their oath-book. The knights wrote the oath-book.
cards.textTemplate: Become Prepared. Draw {draw} card.

upgrade.textTemplate: Become Prepared. Draw {draw} card. Gain {block} Block.

cards.name: Backstep
cards.flavor:
Retreat of the lower-river ice-cutters.

The cutters know which ice beneath the bridges holds and which only seems to, and sell the knowledge by the season. Their map is drawn inside a cutter's coat and passed down with it.

Its present wearer says it has been wrong since the second winter.
cards.textTemplate: Gain {block} Block. Become Prepared.

cards.name: Twin Prick
cards.flavor:
Two small wounds, set close together.

The Court's surgeons recorded them as bites when they found them upon bodies along the bridges. Their receipts give the hour, the bridge and the fee for the inquest. Not one case was closed.

The dock children call it the Surgeon's Signature.
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage {hits} times. Prepared: deal {damage.2} damage {hits.2} times. Consume Prepared.

cards.name: Pocket Sand
cards.flavor:
Kiln ash, carried in a coat lining.

From the south-bank lime kilns, where the dock poor laboured for the Court's builders. The Court paid in lime and taxed in coin; the ash was the one thing given freely.

The kilns went cold with the Court Flame. The ash has not run out.
cards.textTemplate: Gain {block} Block. Apply {weak} Weak.

cards.name: Hamstring
cards.flavor:
Cut behind the knee.

The docks' answer to the stitched knights, who cannot kneel, and once fallen cannot rise. The surgeons called the knights unbending. On the docks, the word is taken as written.

The Fourth Bridge rail bears a tally of knights left upon the ice.
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage. Apply {vulnerable} Vulnerable.

cards.name: Serrated Shiv
cards.flavor:
Shiv sawn from a Marionette's spine-rod.

The Court's surgeons set steel rods in the spines of their dancers, to keep them upright through the dance. Dock thieves call the taking of one a mercy.

The surgeons who fitted them took their reasons beneath the ice.
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage. Apply {bleed} Bleed. Prepared: apply {bleed.2} more. Consume Prepared.

cards.name: Smoke Veil
cards.flavor:
River fog, thickened with ash.

The fog rose off the water the night the Court Flame died, and has not lifted. The Court's lamplighters, paid to burn it away, were the first to be lost in it.

Their guild-book ends with a list of lamps to be relit. None are marked done.
cards.textTemplate: Gain {block} Block. Apply {weak} Weak to ALL enemies.

cards.name: Ricochet
cards.flavor:
Blade skipped across the ice.

A children's game on the frozen river, played with pebbles by the young and knives by the old. The ice keeps no witnesses, they say.

It is said the Marrow Organist, beneath it, hears every throw.
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage to ALL enemies.

cards.name: Low Blow
cards.flavor:
Strike below the belt.

Forbidden by the Court's code of arms, which hangs upon the Citadel gate in frost-bitten gilt. The children of the docks read it aloud to one another in jest.

Its final clause, on the treatment of the unmarked, has been chipped from the stone.
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage and {poiseDamage} Poise damage. Prepared: deal {poiseDamage.2} more Poise damage. Consume Prepared.

cards.name: Pilfer
cards.flavor:
Lift worked in the crowds upon the bridges.

The Court counted wrists and kept careful rolls, but never counted purses. Old Keel, the Tollmouth fence, taught that to rob a courtier sewn to his post was salvage, not theft.

He claimed to have been a courtier once. His wrist bears the brand.
cards.textTemplate: Draw {draw} cards. Discard 1 card at random.

cards.name: Vanish
cards.flavor:
Art of the unmarked beneath the bridges.

Taught to the docks by those who lived under the Citadel's bridges before the Decree, when to be seen was to be entered on a roll. Under the bridges there is nothing but ice.

Most of those teachers vanished in the end. Where to, the docks cannot agree.
cards.textTemplate: Gain {block} Block. Become Prepared. Add a Smoke Pellet to your hand. Exhaust.

upgrade.textTemplate: Gain {block} Block. Become Prepared. Add a Smoke Pellet to your hand.

cards.name: Cheap Shot
cards.flavor:
Blow at the already wounded.

The Tollmouth fence calls it the only honest bargain on the river, and charges for lessons in teeth. He says he learned the practice from a Court magistrate who levied fines the same way.

The jar upon his counter is nearly full.
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage. If the target is Weak, deal {damage.2} more.

cards.name: Blade Dance
cards.flavor:
Cuts in the figure of the Marionettes' dance.

The surgeons stitched the Court's dancers to their dance when the Court Flame died, and they perform upon the frozen river for no one. The dance was meant to end at dawn.

A small Marionette on the Fourth Bridge waits for the ending. Thieves leave her coins.
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage {hits} times. Prepared: deal {damage.2} damage {hits.2} times. Consume Prepared.

cards.name: Garrote
cards.flavor:
Loop of the Court tailors' gilt thread.

Bought cheap on the docks once the tailors had no more use for it. The Court's surgeons bought the same thread, for purposes never shared with the tailors.

The surgeons and the stranglers were ever its best customers.
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage. Apply {bleed} Bleed and {weak} Weak.

cards.name: Fan of Knives
cards.flavor:
Surgeon's roll of scalpels, thrown as one.

The rolls reach the docks more often than their owners, sold by ice-cutters who find them frozen into the river, the coat still about them. The surgeons tried to flee the Citadel on the night of the Burning.

The ice closed over those who ran.
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage to ALL enemies. Draw {draw} card.

cards.name: Setup
cards.flavor:
Preparation of a dock job.

A window left open on the Lantern Bridge, a lamp turned low, a guard paid to cough. The method is credited to a thief called the Wick, who planned the first robbery of the Regent's hall in the years of the Mark Trade.

It is said the Court itself paid her to rob it.
cards.textTemplate: Become Prepared. Gain {gainEnergy} Energy. Add a Shiv to your hand. Exhaust.

upgrade.textTemplate: Become Prepared. Gain {gainEnergy} Energy. Draw {draw} card. Add a Shiv to your hand. Exhaust.

cards.name: Acrobatics
cards.flavor:
The rooftop road of the frozen docks.

Bridge rail, lamp post, gutter, never the street. The Court's watch walked only the paved ways, for the paving had been blessed at the Founding and the rooftops had not.

Whether the watch was pious or idle is not agreed.
cards.textTemplate: Gain {block} Block. Draw {draw} cards. Discard 1 at random.

cards.name: Disorient
cards.flavor:
Spin practised in the Hall of Mirrors.

The Glass Regent's mirrors are the frozen river beneath the bridges, and they show more than stands before them. Thieves who went in for the silver learned to turn a courtier until he lost the throne.

It is said the Regent herself now reigns from the wrong side of the glass.
cards.textTemplate: Apply {weak} Weak and {vulnerable} Vulnerable. Exhaust.

upgrade.textTemplate: Apply {weak} Weak and {vulnerable} Vulnerable.

cards.name: Coup de Grace
cards.flavor:
Finishing thrust of the Court's surgeons.

They called it a courtesy and billed it as a procedure, listed between stitching and funeral in their fee schedule. The docks learned it watching the surgeons at work upon the bridges after the Burning.

The schedule has since been amended by hand. The price has risen.
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage. If the target is Vulnerable, deal {damage.2} more.

cards.name: Sap
cards.flavor:
Sand-weighted cosh of the docks.

Meant to fell without killing. It does not work upon the Marionettes, who dance on with slack strings. One thief used it upon a girl at the foot of the Stitched Throne, a dancer no older than a dock child.

He returned asking whether anyone knew the tune she hummed.
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage. Apply {weak} Weak. Deal {poiseDamage} Poise damage.

cards.name: Shadowstep
cards.flavor:
Step through a pier's shadow.

The shadows beneath the bridges are let by the season, and rent is owed to whoever held the pier before. Tenancies pass down like a trade.

The oldest belongs to one not seen since the Decree. The rent is always paid.
cards.textTemplate: Gain {block} Block. Become Prepared. Draw {draw} card.

cards.name: Afterimage
cards.flavor:
Reflection left in the Regent's glass.

The mirrors of the Hall held a thief's image a heartbeat longer than they should. The Regent's stewards recorded it as the Hall's loyalty.

The glass has grown slower with each winter since the Burning.
cards.textTemplate: Every third card you play grants 3 Block.

cards.name: Bloodletter
cards.flavor:
Bleeding, as the Citadel's surgeons practised it.

Their receipts name the patient, the measure drawn, and the patient's satisfaction, marked on every surviving copy. The surgeons held that bleeding balanced a courtier's humours before an oath.

Receipts from the last month before the Burning bear no names.
cards.textTemplate: Double the target's Bleed. Exhaust.

upgrade.textTemplate: Double the target's Bleed.

cards.name: Venomcoat
cards.flavor:
Sedative paste of the Court's surgeons.

Sold by the vial to courtiers who could not sleep in the weeks before the Decree. The docks found it served a blade as well as a cup of wine.

The label promises a dreamless night.
cards.textTemplate: Apply {venom} Venom. Become Prepared.

cards.name: Misdirect
cards.flavor:
Art of leading the watch astray.

Perfected on the night of the Courtly Decree, when the brand-men came down to the river to mark the last of the unmarked by dawn, and the ice-cutters paid the bridge watch to lead them in circles.

The Decree said dawn. On that side of the river, dawn came late.
cards.textTemplate: Gain {block} Block. Apply {weak} Weak to ALL enemies. Become Prepared.

cards.name: Assassinate
cards.flavor:
Killing blow, struck after a single question.

The way of a dock thief who hunts one particular Court surgeon. The question has been told upon the docks; the surgeon's name has not. Some believe the question concerns a stitching. Others, that the surgeon is kin.

The docks have learned not to ask twice.
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage. Prepared: deal {damage.2} more. Consume Prepared. Exhaust.

cards.name: Thousand Cuts
cards.flavor:
Many small cuts, each undoing a stitch.

The surgeons called it the procedure run backward, and forbade it, for a courtier sewn to his post had sworn an oath. The winter after the Burning, a surgeon was found unstitching his own wife from the palace stair.

The surgeons' day-book records only a failed stitching.
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage {hits} times. Prepared: deal {damage.2} damage {hits.2} times. Consume Prepared.

cards.name: Deadly Tempo
cards.flavor:
Rhythm of the frozen docks.

The dock clock froze at the Burning, its hands upon the King's Hour. Before, thieves timed their work by it, and the Court timed its watch by the same.

Since then the docks keep time by their own pulses, and no two agree.
cards.textTemplate: At the start of your turn, become Prepared and draw a card.

cards.name: Opportunist
cards.flavor:
First law of the frozen docks.

When the knight stumbles, the purse swings. The stitched knights stumble often in their sewn armour, and the docks have prospered by it.

Many of those knights are the fathers and brothers of the docks. This is not spoken of.
cards.textTemplate: Whenever an enemy Staggers, become Prepared and draw a card.

cards.name: Envenom
cards.flavor:
Poison from a surgeon's second shelf.

The second shelf held what the first could not treat. Thieves who entered the surgeons' houses after the Burning found the second shelves full and the first bare.

The apprentices will not say which was emptied first.
cards.textTemplate: Your attacks apply 1 Venom per stack.

cards.name: Toxic Volley
cards.flavor:
Sedative vials, broken into the river fog.

Loosed upwind of the bridge watch, which slept through three robberies. The river smelled of it for weeks.

The watch ledger records those weeks as quiet, and commends the men for their vigilance.
cards.textTemplate: Apply {venom} Venom and {weak} Weak to ALL enemies.

cards.name: Smoke Bomb
cards.flavor:
Pig's bladder of kiln ash.

Split upon the stones, it raises a fog the bridge watch reports as a haunting. The ash is from the south-bank kilns, which in the Court's last years were fired with something other than lime.

The reports are not wholly wrong.
cards.textTemplate: Gain {block} Block. Apply {weak} Weak to ALL enemies. Exhaust.

cards.name: Execution Window
cards.flavor:
The moment the watch looks away.

Every guard has one. In the years of the Mark Trade, the watch's were written into the roster for a fee: the hours each bridge would stand unguarded, and beside each hour, a name.

None of those names appear in any Court record.
cards.textTemplate: Apply {vulnerable} Vulnerable. Become Prepared. Draw {draw} card. Exhaust.

cards.name: Perfect Heist
cards.flavor:
Theft of the Glass Regent's mirrors.

Every mirror is entered in the Hall's inventory, and every one is gone. The older thieves credit the Wick.

The Hall of Mirrors is full of glass to this day. That is how the docks know it was perfect.
cards.textTemplate: Draw {draw} cards. Gain {gainEnergy} Energy. Exhaust.

cards.name: Deathblow
cards.flavor:
Killing stroke of the frozen docks.

Struck where the river keeps what the surgeons leave. The river does not thaw, the docks say, because it is full, and the Court built more bridges rather than ask why.

Beneath the ice the Marrow Organist plays the funeral service. He has never reached its end.
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage. If the target has Bleed, deal {damage.2} more. If it has Venom, deal {damage.3} more.

cards.name: Prepare
cards.flavor:
Hands warmed before the work.

Cold hands drop knives. Dock children learn to warm their hands before they learn to steal, and never at a fire another has lit. A borrowed fire is a debt, and the docks collect.

The fires on the Citadel side burn more than wood.
cards.textTemplate: Become Prepared. Exhaust.

upgrade.textTemplate: Become Prepared.

cards.name: Pinning Shot
cards.flavor:
An arrow through the hem, not the heart.

Dock archers learned it on the gulls first, then on the Court's bailiffs, whose long coats caught on every piling. A pinned bailiff is a patient one.

The docks still tell which bailiff wore the longest coat, and laugh.
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage. Apply {weak} Weak.

cards.name: Arrow Volley
cards.flavor:
Loose, nock, loose again.

The dock crews kept a barrel of salvaged arrows beneath every stair, few of them straight. A volley did not need them straight, only many and quick, and the crews were both.

The barrels are empty now. Nobody admits to refilling them.
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage to ALL enemies {hits} times.

cards.name: Nock and Wait
cards.flavor:
The string drawn, the breath held.

A dock archer waits for the tide bell, when every head on the quay turns at once. The bell has rung at the wrong hours since the Burning.

The archers have learned to wait for the heads instead.
cards.textTemplate: Draw {draw} cards. Become Prepared.

cards.name: Aimed Shot
cards.flavor:
One arrow, one seam in the armour.

The stitched knights of the Court wear plate sewn at the joints, and the stitching is the weak place. A dock archer who knows a surgeon's work knows where to aim.

Some of them learned it on the surgeons' tables.
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage. Prepared: deal {damage.2} more and apply {vulnerable} Vulnerable. Consume Prepared.

cards.name: Barbed Arrow
cards.flavor:
A head filed backward so it will not come out.

Fishhook smiths on the docks made them in secret, for the Court forbade barbs after a bailiff died of one. The smiths still make fishhooks.

The fish on the docks are said to be larger than they were.
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage. Apply {bleed} Bleed.

cards.name: Binding Parry
cards.flavor:
The blade caught, turned, and held aside.

A duelling master of the Court taught it for coin to anyone who asked, dock thieves among them. When the Court learned whom he had taught, it stitched his hands.

He teaches it still, by describing it.
cards.textTemplate: Gain {block} Block. Become Prepared. Draw {draw} card.

cards.name: Whirling Guard
cards.flavor:
A spin that is both parry and cut.

Dock dancers performed it for the Court at feast days, with painted wooden knives. After the Burning they were seen performing it on the quay, with other knives, and without the paint.

No feast has been held since.
cards.textTemplate: Gain {block} Block. Deal {damage} damage {hits} times.

cards.name: Draw Cut
cards.flavor:
Single cut from the scabbard, as it is done beyond the marches.

The curved blades reached the ring in the years of the Mark Trade, borne by foreign lords who paid to be warm there. They burned with the rest of the marked, far from home, and left their swords where they fell.

The merchant knows whose each one was. He sells that separately.
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage. Apply {bleed} Bleed.

cards.name: Sundering Hew
cards.flavor:
Hew of a Court knight's greatsword.

Too heavy to carry far, and too dear to leave. The corrupted knights pause at the sight of one in a Forsaken's hands, unable to believe an unmarked hand holds their steel.

That pause is worth the weight.
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage and {poiseDamage} Poise damage.

cards.name: Honed Edge
cards.flavor:
Whetstone from the cairn.

At the Grave of the Nameless, the custom is to take one and leave one. The stones are weald sandstone, marches slate, black glass of the reach. One is starstone.

Within the year, someone always carries it back.
cards.textTemplate: Gain {strength} Strength. Exhaust.

cards.name: Iron Skin
cards.flavor:
Plate of cold iron, worn where a flame-mark would lie.

First worn by the ice-fishers of the Pale Marches in the year of the Decree, when the Court's brand-men came for the unmarked. Such plates are left upon the Grave of the Nameless for those who climb after.

Most have been worn thin by more than one wearer.
cards.textTemplate: Gain {block} Block.

cards.name: Field Dressing
cards.flavor:
Clean rag, tied to the cairn.

Boiled by someone who expected to need it, and did not return for it. The custom reached the hamlets with Chapel refugees after the Burning; the hamlets kept the custom, and let the prayer go.

Some rags arrive embroidered with names. The hamlets unpick them.
cards.textTemplate: Heal {heal} HP. Exhaust.

cards.name: Hex
cards.flavor:
Sign scratched upon a door.

The hamlets mark it on houses where someone marked burns slowly within, to keep it from coming out. They learned the sign from the Chapel, which set it upon the houses of the unmarked before the Decree.

The hamlets call it fair to use it the other way round.
cards.textTemplate: Apply {weak} Weak and {vulnerable} Vulnerable. Exhaust.

cards.name: Transmute
cards.flavor:
Cinder spent in the palm.

For a moment, the hand that holds it does not shake. The hamlets hold that each cinder was someone once, and forbid spending a cinder one took oneself.

Those who return from the ring have mostly broken that rule.
cards.textTemplate: Gain {gainEnergy} Energy. Draw {draw} card. Exhaust.

cards.name: Twin Fang
cards.flavor:
Two knives, worn crosswise.

One for the hound, one for its handler. The weald's blight-hounds were the Wardens' before the Burning, and run yet with Bastion kennelmen who turned with the pack.

A handler may be reasoned with, briefly. Never twice.
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage {hits} times.

cards.name: Blinding Sand
cards.flavor:
Ash thrown in the eyes.

The hamlets learned in the first winter that what came out of the weald flinched from ash as the living do. Some took this as proof the corrupted could be saved.

Marl's Hollow took it as proof they could be blinded. Marl's Hollow endures.
cards.textTemplate: Apply {weak} Weak to ALL enemies. Exhaust.

cards.name: Hamstring
cards.flavor:
