Cut at the back of the leg.

Taught upon the road with a single instruction: all things of the ring walk, so go for the legs. The saying is scratched on cairns from the weald to the coast, weeks apart.

It is cut in the same hand on every one.
cards.textTemplate: Apply {vulnerable} Vulnerable to ALL enemies. Exhaust.

cards.name: Master of Strategy
cards.flavor:
Maps scratched upon cairn stones.

Left by climbers who came back down, or meant to. The hamlet councils copy the true ones and burn the rest, and each winter argue which were which.

The oldest shows a fourth road leading off the ring toward the coast. It has not been burned.
cards.textTemplate: Draw {draw} cards. Exhaust.

cards.name: Bashing Blow
cards.flavor:
Blow of whatever is heavy.

A cudgel, a mallet, a shovel from a mine camp. The reach's miners swing it at things in the lower galleries that were miners once. Foreman Coll says not to look at their hands, which remember the work.

His camp has lost fewer than any other.
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage and {poiseDamage} Poise damage.

cards.name: Quick Guard
cards.flavor:
Arm raised upon the viaduct.

The viaducts are older than the kingdom, and have no rails. Climbers say they were built to carry heat, not people. Those who cross learn to keep one arm raised against the wind.

The stone has never learned to expect feet.
cards.textTemplate: Gain {block} Block. Draw {draw} card. Exhaust.

cards.name: Sweeping Blow
cards.flavor:
Wide swing for the viaduct.

Where the corrupted come three abreast and the stone is narrow. The Forsaken councils teach that the viaducts were always built to funnel something, long before there were corrupted to funnel.

The corrupted walk them because the stone expects a crowd.
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage to ALL enemies.

cards.name: Enfeeble
cards.flavor:
Sea salt, rubbed into a wound.

The ship-breakers swear by it. Salt, they say, is the one thing upon the ring the fire has never touched, for nothing written survives the sea.

They have not seen what the Tidebound Abbey keeps in its boathouse.
cards.textTemplate: Apply {vulnerable} Vulnerable to ALL enemies. Exhaust.

cards.name: Colossus Smash
cards.flavor:
Blow at the joints of something vast.

Learned against the Goldbough Avatar, the heraldic idol kneeling in a clearing of the weald, a sapling grown through it. It does not know the kingdom is gone.

It is carved stone and gilt. It flinches all the same.
cards.textTemplate: Deal {damage} damage. Apply {vulnerable} Vulnerable.

cards.name: Wound
cards.textTemplate: Unplayable.
cards.flavor:
A cut that closed wrong.

It knits into a hard ridge that aches before the weather turns. Climbers call it the road keeping its share.

The hamlets' older word for it means owed.

cards.name: Dazed
cards.textTemplate: Unplayable. Ethereal.
cards.flavor:
Light behind the eyes, left by a Grave Wisp.

Those who have seen a wisp up close say it looked at them as if reading.

Close your eyes. Do not speak your name until the light is gone.

cards.name: Slimed
cards.textTemplate: Exhaust.
cards.flavor:
Grey muck from the drowned hamlet.

It clings, and will not wash out in cold water. The hamlet flooded before the Burning, in a flood the Wardens called natural.

It is warmer than anything in the weald has a right to be.

cards.name: Guilt
cards.textTemplate: Unplayable. At the end of your turn, if this is in your hand, lose {loseHp} HP.
cards.flavor:
What follows looting at the Second Cairn.

The second time is easier. That is how climbers know the ring has begun on them.

cards.name: Rallying Banner
cards.textTemplate: An ally gains {block} Block.
cards.flavor:
Blank rag upon a pole.

Planted where climbers who meet upon the road may find one another. The Forsaken never had banners, for a banner bears a name. The corrupted come to them too.

A rag on a pole. Find it. Stand by it.

cards.name: Shared Flame
cards.textTemplate: An ally heals {heal} HP. Exhaust.
cards.flavor:
Warmth passed between two climbers.

Hands over one coal, breath beneath one coat, with no hearth and no ledger. The Chapel would have named it theft. It is the only warmth upon the ring owed to no one.

Warmth passed between two outlives the fire.

cards.name: Oath of Ash
cards.textTemplate: An ally gains {strength} Strength; you gain {strength.2}. Exhaust.
cards.flavor:
Oath sworn in ash.

A smear upon each other's wrist, where the mark would have been; no witness, no name. It binds twice, once for each. The Court held that an unwitnessed oath binds no one.

The Court is sewn to its oaths now.

cards.name: Guardian
cards.flavor:
Kite shield of the Court's knights, its strap cut short.

Such shields lie easily found upon the marches road, where the knights who bore them were stitched to their posts and left standing. Climbers take the shields and leave the knights.

The knights have not objected.
cards.textTemplate: Gain {block} Block. Add a temporary Enter: Bulwark to your hand. It costs 1 Energy and Exhausts. Exhaust.

cards.name: Enter: Bulwark
cards.flavor:
The Wardens' holding stance, learned from the shield.

A shield that stood in the Bastion's line keeps the habit, the elders say, and pulls the arm into place. They call it superstition.

They tell climbers to carry Bastion shields, and never Court ones.
cards.textTemplate: Enter Bulwark Stance. Exhaust.

upgrade.textTemplate: Enter Bulwark Stance. Gain {block} extra Block. Exhaust.

cards.name: Bastion
cards.flavor:
Tower shield from the Bastion's walls.

Heavy as a door, nearly as tall. The Wardens set such shields in the embrasures to fight from, never to carry. Climbers carry them regardless, for a moving wall is better than a still one.

The weight bows the bearer forward, as the Wardens once bowed before the Bastion.

Shield with nails driven through the boss.

The nails are from the Bastion's own gates. It is said a sellsword made it on the night of the Burning, from the gate he was hired to hold. His name is not known.

No bearer since has drawn the nails.

cards.flavor:
Frost spear of the Pale Marches.

Its point was reforged from the broken blade of a Court knight, and marches steel keeps its frost long after leaving the cold. The ice-fishers who made it say the knight gave the blade freely, before the Decree, for a winter's fish.

The ice-fishers keep no records.

cards.flavor:
Axe of the Dead Foundry.

The Foundry's fires went out with the Crown Flame, and its forges have been warm ever since, though none has lit them. Corran, a foundryman, broke this axe from a cold mould at dawn and carried it up the Basalt Stair.

He says no one poured it.

Ward of the Chapel's evening bell-ringers.

A chime rung at vespers to close the day. Its bell was taken long ago; only the frame and the ward remain. Climbers who carry it say it rings at dusk regardless.

A Chapel ward, rung at vespers. The bell is gone.
